easy: A part of a building with walls, a floor, and a ceiling.

ex.en: My room has a bed, a desk, and many books.
ex.ko: 내 방에는 침대와 책상, 그리고 많은 책이 있다.

easy: Empty space where you can move or put things.

ex.en: Please make room for me on the bench.
ex.ko: 벤치에 내 자리를 좀 만들어 줘.

easy: A chance for something to happen.

ex.en: There is still room for improvement in my drawing.
ex.ko: 내 그림은 아직 나아질 여지가 있다.

easy: More than two, but not a lot.

ex.en: Several kids brought their dogs to the park.
ex.ko: 몇몇 아이들이 공원에 강아지를 데려왔다.

easy: A big school that people go to after high school to learn more.

ex.en: My big sister goes to a university far from home.
ex.ko: 우리 누나는 집에서 먼 대학교에 다닌다.

easy: To do better than everyone else in a game or race.

ex.en: Our team won the soccer game.
ex.ko: 우리 팀이 축구 경기에서 이겼다.

easy: To get something by working hard.

ex.en: She won her teacher's trust by working hard.
ex.ko: 그녀는 열심히 노력해서 선생님의 믿음을 얻었다.

easy: Not right; having a mistake in it.

ex.en: My answer on the math test was wrong.
ex.ko: 수학 시험에서 내 답이 틀렸다.

easy: Bad or unfair; something you should not do.

ex.en: It is wrong to take things that are not yours.
ex.ko: 남의 물건을 가져가는 것은 옳지 않다.

easy: Not the right one for the time or place.

ex.en: Flip-flops are the wrong shoes for a snowy day.
ex.ko: 눈 오는 날에 슬리퍼는 맞지 않는 신발이다.

easy: Together with someone.

ex.en: My little brother came along to the park.
ex.ko: 남동생이 나와 함께 공원에 따라왔다.

easy: A young female person.

ex.en: The girl on my team scored two goals.
ex.ko: 우리 팀의 소녀가 두 골을 넣었다.

easy: A female child.

ex.en: That little girl is learning to ride a bike.
ex.ko: 저 여자아이는 자전거 타는 법을 배우고 있다.

easy: A female child of a mom and dad.

ex.en: Grandma has two boys and one girl.
ex.ko: 할머니에게는 아들 둘과 딸 하나가 있다.

easy: Nice to look at in a soft, gentle way.

ex.en: She wore a pretty dress with little flowers.
ex.ko: 그녀는 작은 꽃무늬가 있는 예쁜 원피스를 입었다.

easy: More than a little, but not completely.

ex.en: The test was pretty easy.
ex.ko: 시험은 꽤 쉬웠다.

easy: To have something from the past come back to your mind.

ex.en: I remember my first day of school.
ex.ko: 나는 학교 첫날을 기억한다.

easy: To keep something in your mind so you do not forget it.

ex.en: Remember to bring your lunch box tomorrow.
ex.ko: 내일 도시락 가져오는 걸 잊지 마.

easy: To think about happy or special times from long ago.

ex.en: Grandpa remembers playing in the river as a boy.
ex.ko: 할아버지는 어린 시절 강에서 놀던 것을 회상하신다.

easy: What we breathe; the invisible stuff all around us.

ex.en: Fresh air feels good after a long day in class.
ex.ko: 수업이 긴 하루를 보내고 나면 신선한 공기가 기분 좋다.

easy: The open space above the ground, up in the sky.

ex.en: The ball flew high up in the air.
ex.ko: 공이 공중 높이 날아올랐다.

easy: A special feeling that a person or place gives off.

ex.en: The old house had a spooky air.
ex.ko: 그 오래된 집에는 으스스한 분위기가 있었다.

easy: A small amount of something.

ex.en: I put a bit of sugar in my milk.
ex.ko: 나는 우유에 설탕을 조금 넣었다.

easy: A tiny piece that broke off something bigger.

ex.en: A bit of the cookie fell on the floor.
ex.ko: 쿠키 조각이 바닥에 떨어졌다.

easy: Someone you know well and like and trust.

ex.en: My best friend sits next to me in class.
ex.ko: 내 단짝 친구는 교실에서 내 옆에 앉는다.

easy: Someone you know a little, but not very well.

ex.en: He is just a friend I know from the bus.
ex.ko: 그는 버스에서 알게 된 그냥 아는 사이일 뿐이다.

easy: To swing at a ball so that it goes far.

ex.en: He hit the ball over the fence.
ex.ko: 그는 공을 쳐서 울타리 너머로 넘겼다.

easy: To bump into something fast and hard.

ex.en: The bike hit a rock and I fell off.
ex.ko: 자전거가 돌에 부딪쳐서 나는 넘어졌다.

easy: To give something a hard knock with your hand or a tool.

ex.en: Dad hit the nail with a hammer.
ex.ko: 아빠는 망치로 못을 쳤다.

easy: Good and pleasant; making you feel happy.

ex.en: We had a nice picnic by the lake.
ex.ko: 우리는 호숫가에서 멋진 소풍을 했다.

easy: Making music with an instrument.

ex.en: Her playing of the piano made everyone clap.
ex.ko: 그녀의 피아노 연주에 모두가 박수를 쳤다.

easy: Having fun by taking part in a game or sport.

ex.en: Playing tag at recess is my favorite.
ex.ko: 쉬는 시간에 술래잡기 놀이를 하는 게 제일 좋다.

easy: Acting out a part in a play or show.

ex.en: Her playing of the queen in the school play was great.
ex.ko: 학교 연극에서 여왕을 맡은 그녀의 연기는 훌륭했다.

easy: Most likely; it will almost surely happen.

ex.en: It will probably rain, so take an umbrella.
ex.ko: 아마 비가 올 테니 우산을 가져가.

easy: A word or group of words people use in some situation.

ex.en: "Piece of cake" is a saying that means very easy.
ex.ko: '식은 죽 먹기'는 아주 쉽다는 뜻의 표현이다.

easy: To know what something means.

ex.en: I understand how to do the math problem now.
ex.ko: 이제 그 수학 문제를 어떻게 푸는지 이해했다.

easy: To suddenly get an idea in your mind.

ex.en: Now I understand why the plant died: it had no water.
ex.ko: 이제 식물이 왜 죽었는지 알겠다. 물이 없었기 때문이다.

easy: To know what the words in a language mean.

ex.en: My grandma understands English but speaks Korean.
ex.ko: 할머니는 영어를 알아들으시지만 한국어로 말씀하신다.

easy: A group of students who learn together.

ex.en: Our class went on a field trip to the zoo.
ex.ko: 우리 반은 동물원으로 현장학습을 갔다.

easy: To move something so it covers an opening.

ex.en: Please close the door when you leave.
ex.ko: 나갈 때 문을 닫아 주세요.

easy: To shut by itself.

ex.en: The door closed behind us with a loud bang.
ex.ko: 문이 쾅 하고 우리 뒤에서 닫혔다.

easy: To stop working as a business or place.

ex.en: The old toy store had to close last year.
ex.ko: 그 오래된 장난감 가게는 작년에 문을 닫아야 했다.

easy: What you plan to do.

ex.en: My idea is to build a treehouse this summer.
ex.ko: 올여름에 나무 위 집을 짓는 게 내 계획이야.

easy: What you think about something.

ex.en: I have an idea that it will snow tomorrow.
ex.ko: 내일 눈이 올 것 같다는 생각이 든다.

easy: Having to do with many countries.

ex.en: The school held an international food day.
ex.ko: 학교에서 국제 음식의 날 행사를 열었다.

easy: The time that came before now.

ex.en: In the past, people wrote letters instead of texting.
ex.ko: 과거에는 사람들이 문자 대신 편지를 썼다.

easy: The form of a verb that tells what already happened.

ex.en: "Ran" is the past of "run".
ex.ko: 'ran'은 'run'의 과거형이다.

easy: Able to happen or be done.

ex.en: It is possible to see stars on a clear night.
ex.ko: 맑은 밤에는 별을 볼 수 있다.

easy: Might happen later.

ex.en: A possible problem is that we may run out of snacks.
ex.ko: 우리 간식이 떨어질 수도 있다는 것이 문제가 될 수 있다.

easy: Wished for and hoped to get.

ex.en: He finally got the wanted bike for his birthday.
ex.ko: 그는 생일에 마침내 갖고 싶던 자전거를 받았다.

easy: Expected to arrive at a certain time.

ex.en: The bus is due at eight o'clock.
ex.ko: 버스는 8시에 도착할 예정이다.

easy: Feeling glad and full of joy.

ex.en: I was so happy when I saw my grandma.
ex.ko: 할머니를 봤을 때 나는 정말 행복했다.

easy: Glad and ready to help.

ex.en: I am happy to help you carry your bag.
ex.ko: 네 가방 드는 걸 기꺼이 도와줄게.

easy: Having to do with people.

ex.en: Making mistakes is a human thing to do.
ex.ko: 실수하는 것은 인간적인 일이다.

easy: Having to do with people, not animals.

ex.en: A human heart beats about 100,000 times a day.
ex.ko: 사람의 심장은 하루에 약 10만 번 뛴다.

easy: Like a person and not like an animal.

ex.en: The robot had a human shape, with two arms and two legs.
ex.ko: 그 로봇은 팔 두 개와 다리 두 개가 있는 사람 모양이었다.

easy: To go from one place to another.

ex.en: The train started to move slowly.
ex.ko: 기차가 천천히 움직이기 시작했다.

easy: To put something in a new place.

ex.en: Can you move your backpack off my seat?
ex.ko: 네 가방을 내 자리에서 좀 옮겨 줄래?

easy: To change how your body or a part of it is placed.

ex.en: The cat moved its tail when it saw the bird.
ex.ko: 고양이는 새를 보자 꼬리를 움직였다.

easy: Something you ask because you want to know.

ex.en: I raised my hand to ask a question.
ex.ko: 나는 질문하려고 손을 들었다.

easy: A problem or topic that people talk about.

ex.en: The question is how we get to the park.
ex.ko: 문제는 우리가 공원에 어떻게 가느냐이다.

easy: A sentence that asks for an answer.

ex.en: "What is your name?" is a question.
ex.ko: '이름이 뭐니?'는 의문문이다.

easy: Things that come one after another in order.

ex.en: We had a series of rainy days in a row.
ex.ko: 비 오는 날이 연달아 이어졌다.

easy: A show with many parts that tell a story over time.

ex.en: My favorite cartoon series has ten episodes.
ex.ko: 내가 제일 좋아하는 만화 시리즈는 10화까지 있다.

easy: To stay somewhere until something happens.

ex.en: We wait for the bus every morning.
ex.ko: 우리는 매일 아침 버스를 기다린다.

easy: A grown-up female person.

ex.en: A woman in a blue coat is our new teacher.
ex.ko: 파란 코트를 입은 여자분이 우리 새 선생님이다.

easy: To say that you want something from someone.

ex.en: I asked my mom for a snack.
ex.ko: 나는 엄마에게 간식을 달라고 했다.

easy: To say a question to someone to get an answer.

ex.en: Ask your teacher if you do not understand.
ex.ko: 이해가 안 되면 선생님께 물어봐.

easy: Near the end of a time period, like the end of the day.

ex.en: We ate dinner late in the evening.
ex.ko: 우리는 저녁 늦게 밥을 먹었다.

easy: Coming after the time it should.

ex.en: I was late for school because I missed the bus.
ex.ko: 버스를 놓쳐서 학교에 늦었다.

easy: To go away from a place.

ex.en: The bus leaves at eight o'clock.
ex.ko: 버스는 8시에 떠난다.

easy: To go away and not take something with you.

ex.en: I left my lunch box on the bus.
ex.ko: 나는 버스에 도시락통을 두고 내렸다.

easy: The direction toward the top of a map.

ex.en: A compass needle points north.
ex.ko: 나침반 바늘은 북쪽을 가리킨다.

easy: The upper part of a country or place.

ex.en: It is colder in the north of the country.
ex.ko: 그 나라의 북부는 더 춥다.

easy: The way you go to head toward the top of a map.

ex.en: We walked north along the river.
ex.ko: 우리는 강을 따라 북쪽으로 걸었다.

easy: A tool with sharp teeth for cutting wood.

ex.en: Dad used a saw to cut the board.
ex.ko: 아빠는 톱으로 판자를 잘랐다.

easy: A machine that cuts wood fast.

ex.en: The saw made a loud noise as it cut the wood.
ex.ko: 전기톱이 나무를 자르며 큰 소리를 냈다.

easy: Better or different from what is usual.

ex.en: My birthday is a special day for me.
ex.ko: 내 생일은 나에게 특별한 날이다.

easy: To look at something carefully for a while.

ex.en: We watch a basketball game every Friday.
ex.ko: 우리는 금요일마다 농구 경기를 본다.

easy: To look after someone or something so they stay safe.

ex.en: Please watch my little sister at the pool.
ex.ko: 수영장에서 내 동생을 잘 지켜봐 줘.

easy: To look at a show or movie.

ex.en: We watch a movie on Saturday nights.
ex.ko: 우리는 토요일 밤마다 영화를 본다.

easy: Also, used after a sentence with "not".

ex.en: I don't like peas, and my brother doesn't either.
ex.ko: 나는 완두콩을 안 좋아하고, 내 동생도 안 좋아한다.

easy: Still to come; not here yet.

ex.en: I wrote a letter to my future self.
ex.ko: 나는 미래의 나에게 편지를 썼다.

easy: Small in amount; not much.

ex.en: The store has low prices this week.
ex.ko: 이번 주에는 가게 가격이 낮다.

easy: Not high; close to the ground.

ex.en: The table is low, so even a baby can reach it.
ex.ko: 그 탁자는 낮아서 아기도 손이 닿는다.

easy: Quiet and soft; not loud.

ex.en: We spoke in low voices so the baby could sleep.
ex.ko: 아기가 잘 수 있도록 우리는 낮은 목소리로 말했다.

easy: The number 1,000,000, which is a thousand thousands.

ex.en: Our city has about a million people.
ex.ko: 우리 도시에는 백만 명 정도가 산다.

easy: The first part of the day, from sunrise until noon.

ex.en: I eat cereal every morning before school.
ex.ko: 나는 매일 아침 학교 가기 전에 시리얼을 먹는다.

easy: The group of officers whose job is to keep people safe.

ex.en: The police helped us cross the busy street.
ex.ko: 경찰이 우리가 붐비는 길을 건너도록 도와주었다.

easy: Lasting only a little time.

ex.en: The movie was short, so we watched it twice.
ex.ko: 영화가 짧아서 우리는 두 번 봤다.

easy: Not long; having a small length.

ex.en: My dog has short legs.
ex.ko: 우리 강아지는 다리가 짧다.

easy: Not tall.

ex.en: I am short, so I stand in front for class photos.
ex.ko: 나는 키가 작아서 단체 사진에서 앞에 선다.

easy: To keep being the same way.

ex.en: Please stay calm during the fire drill.
ex.ko: 소방 훈련 때는 침착함을 유지하세요.

easy: To be in a place and not leave.

ex.en: I stay at my grandma's house on weekends.
ex.ko: 나는 주말마다 할머니 집에 머문다.

easy: To live in a place for a short time as a guest.

ex.en: My cousin will stay with us for a week.
ex.ko: 사촌이 우리 집에서 일주일 묵을 거야.

easy: How old someone or something is.

ex.en: My dog's age is seven.
ex.ko: 우리 강아지의 나이는 일곱 살이다.

easy: A long part of history that had something special about it.

ex.en: The Stone Age was long before cars.
ex.ko: 석기 시대는 자동차가 생기기 훨씬 전이었다.

easy: How old you must be to do something.

ex.en: At the age of six, I started school.
ex.ko: 여섯 살 때 나는 학교에 들어갔다.

easy: To give money to get something.

ex.en: I bought a new notebook at the store.
ex.ko: 나는 가게에서 새 공책을 샀다.

easy: To be enough money to get something.

ex.en: Five dollars can buy a big slice of pizza.
ex.ko: 5달러면 큰 피자 한 조각을 살 수 있다.

easy: To do what is needed to fix a problem.

ex.en: Mom showed me how to deal with a stuck zipper.
ex.ko: 엄마는 지퍼가 낀 것을 어떻게 처리하는지 보여 주셨다.

easy: The color of strawberries, tomatoes, and fire trucks.

ex.en: She wore red boots in the rain.
ex.ko: 그녀는 빗속에서 빨간 장화를 신었다.

easy: Having a face that turns pink or red.

ex.en: My face went red when everyone sang happy birthday.
ex.ko: 모두가 생일 축하 노래를 부르자 내 얼굴이 빨개졌다.

easy: A paper that tells what someone learned.

ex.en: I wrote a report about sea turtles.
ex.ko: 나는 바다거북에 대한 보고서를 썼다.

easy: A short story in the news about what happened.

ex.en: The news report said it would snow tomorrow.
ex.ko: 뉴스 보도에서 내일 눈이 올 거라고 했다.

easy: In a short time from now.

ex.en: Dinner will be ready soon.
ex.ko: 저녁이 곧 준비될 거야.

easy: One of three equal parts.

ex.en: I ate a third of the pizza.
ex.ko: 나는 피자의 3분의 1을 먹었다.

easy: The player who guards the base before home plate.

ex.en: My brother plays third for his baseball team.
ex.ko: 우리 형은 야구팀에서 3루수를 맡고 있다.

easy: Number three in order.

ex.en: I came in third in the race.
ex.ko: 나는 달리기에서 3등을 했다.

easy: To face a different way.

ex.en: Turn around and look at the rainbow.
ex.ko: 돌아서서 무지개를 봐.

easy: To change into something different.

ex.en: Leaves turn red and yellow in the fall.
ex.ko: 가을에는 나뭇잎이 빨갛고 노랗게 변한다.

easy: To look at something to see if it is right or working.

ex.en: Dad checks the tires before a trip.
ex.ko: 아빠는 여행 전에 타이어를 점검하신다.

easy: To look into something to find out about it.

ex.en: Let's check the map to find the zoo.
ex.ko: 지도를 확인해서 동물원을 찾아보자.

easy: To make sure something is done or true.

ex.en: Check that the lights are off before you leave.
ex.ko: 나가기 전에 불이 꺼졌는지 확인해.

easy: Making something better or bigger step by step.

ex.en: The team worked on the development of a new game.
ex.ko: 팀은 새 게임을 개발하는 일에 매달렸다.

easy: Slowly changing and growing into something more advanced.

ex.en: The development of a butterfly takes several weeks.
ex.ko: 나비의 발달에는 몇 주가 걸린다.

easy: The way a living thing grows and changes over time.

ex.en: A baby's development is fast in the first year.
ex.ko: 아기는 첫 해에 빠르게 발달한다.

easy: A kind or type of something.

ex.en: Soccer is a form of exercise.
ex.ko: 축구는 운동의 한 종류다.

easy: Also; and more than that.

ex.en: He said he was tired, and further, he was hungry.
ex.ko: 그는 피곤하고, 게다가 배도 고프다고 했다.

easy: At a greater distance away.

ex.en: The school is further down the road.
ex.ko: 학교는 길을 따라 더 멀리 있다.

easy: A written record of what people said at a meeting.

ex.en: The class secretary wrote the minutes of our meeting.
ex.ko: 학급 서기가 우리 회의의 회의록을 썼다.

easy: To do something.

ex.en: Think before you act.
ex.ko: 행동하기 전에 생각해라.

easy: To show how you are by what you do.

ex.en: Try to act kindly to new classmates.
ex.ko: 새 친구에게 친절하게 행동하려고 노력해라.

easy: To pretend to be someone in a play or movie.

ex.en: I will act as a pirate in the school play.
